access_time_basis: Access timestamps below record the UTC start of the direct retrieval pass for these source pages; 2026-10-10T05:01:19Z. Retrieved via web open/search. No building or field data were accessed.

records.title: ISO 1996-2:2017 — Environmental noise determination of sound pressure levels
records.released_version: Edition 3, July 2017; official page summary says reviewed/confirmed and current in 2026; lifecycle also lists 2026-04-01 'to be revised' and 2026-05-20 'confirmed' entries.
records.locator: ISO product record: abstract, status, and lifecycle; outdoor applicability and uncertainty statement.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO official product page and read its scope/status preview.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The method is primarily for outdoor environmental sound; user-selected measurement effort determines uncertainty and uncertainty is reported. The record does not set a universal allowable maximum uncertainty. The page's summary and lifecycle contain both a current/confirmed statement and a 2026 revision entry; check the official lifecycle again before standards-compliance use.
records.applicability: Framework for a separately defined courtyard sound outcome and scenario comparison; it does not identify the building path, select a neighbor threshold, or establish local legal compliance.

records.title: ISO 16283-1:2014 — Field measurement of airborne sound insulation between rooms
records.released_version: Edition 1, February 2014, Amendment 1:2017; official page says the 2014 edition was reviewed and confirmed in 2025.
records.locator: ISO product record: abstract, amendment listing, status/lifecycle.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO official product page and read the method scope, frequency/volume range, amendment, and current-status record.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Airborne insulation between two rooms; stated intended volume 10–250 m³ and frequency range 50 Hz–5 kHz. The result is frequency-dependent. It is not a structural-vibration method.
records.applicability: Helps distinguish a possible room-to-room airborne follow-up from courtyard/environmental measurement. Its stated frequency floor and two-room scope are material limits for low-bass/exterior questions.

records.title: ISO 16283-3:2016 — Field measurement of façade sound insulation
records.released_version: Edition 1, February 2016; official lifecycle says published and to be revised, with ISO/CD 16283-3 under development.
records.locator: ISO product record: abstract, published/status and replacement lifecycle.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO official product page and read the façade method scope and revision status.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Airborne façade-element and whole-façade insulation methods for rooms 10–250 m³ and 50 Hz–5 kHz. Published but marked to be revised; it is not the same measurement as ambient courtyard sound.
records.applicability: A method reference if later façade transmission is investigated with suitable equipment; not a low-frequency structural test and not evidence of this façade's performance.

records.title: ISO 10052:2021 — Field survey method for airborne/impact insulation and service-equipment sound
records.locator: OBP introduction, scope, survey procedure, and precision notes.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO Online Browsing Platform record; read the introduction, scope, and references to engineering methods.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Survey method simplifies field measurements using a handheld sound-level instrument and a manual microphone sweep; insulation is in octave bands. It is intended for dwelling/comparable rooms up to 150 m³ and has higher a priori uncertainty than engineering-level methods. Annex operating cycles apply only when consistent with national requirements.
records.applicability: Supports using a handheld meter only for a bounded screening plan; does not make a basic meter, phone, or improvised music test a formal insulation assessment.

records.title: ISO 3382-2:2008 — Reverberation time in ordinary rooms
records.released_version: Edition 1, June 2008; corrigendum 1:2009; official record says reviewed/confirmed in 2022.
records.locator: ISO product record: abstract and lifecycle; method procedure, apparatus, positions, data evaluation/reporting.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO official product page and reviewed its description and status.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Specifies methods for measuring reverberation time in ordinary rooms; reported results may inform room requirements and corrections to other acoustic measurements.
records.applicability: Internal room-decay/room-acoustics outcome only; a shorter reverberation time is not proof of less sound in the courtyard.

records.title: ISO 23591:2021 — Acoustic quality criteria for music rehearsal rooms and spaces
records.released_version: Edition 1, September 2021, Amendment 1:2025 (Asian/Korean traditional music); official page lifecycle shows review activity in 2026.
records.locator: ISO product record: abstract, amendment, and lifecycle; scope excludes sound-insulation criteria.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO official product page and read its scope/status preview.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Differentiates rehearsal-room acoustic criteria by amplified, quiet acoustic, and loud acoustic music and includes room height/volume/area. It can be used to assess existing-room suitability. The document explicitly does not include sound-insulation criteria; current lifecycle is under review.
records.applicability: Use only after identifying actual music types and room dimensions, to frame the in-room result. Do not use it to infer neighbor disturbance or façade performance.

records.title: Pedersen, Møller & Persson Waye, Indoor Measurements of Noise at Low Frequencies — Problems and Solutions
records.released_version: Journal of Low Frequency Noise, Vibration and Active Control, vol. 26, issue 4, pp. 249–270, 2007; DOI 10.1260/026309207783571389.
records.locator: Publisher abstract and paper sections describing standing-wave spatial variation and comparison of Swedish/Danish measurement methods across three rooms.
records.observed_operation: Opened the publisher journal page; read the abstract and bibliographic record.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The reported 20–30 dB spatial variation is low-frequency room behavior demonstrated by simulations and measurements in three rooms. The authors discuss measurement-position methods and their risk of missing high-level locations.
records.applicability: Supports several fixed room microphone positions and explicit uncertainty; its magnitude is not a prediction for this building.

records.title: Løvholt, Norén-Cosgriff, Madshus & Ellingsen, Simulating low frequency sound transmission through walls and windows by a two-way coupled fluid-structure interaction model
records.released_version: Journal of Sound and Vibration, vol. 396, pp. 203–216, 2017; DOI 10.1016/j.jsv.2017.02.026.
records.locator: Publisher abstract: experimental/model range 10–100 Hz, role of structural connections, wall/window contributions.
records.observed_operation: Retrieved the publisher abstract/search record for the primary paper.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The paper compares finite-element fluid-structure simulations with laboratory experiments for plain walls and walls with windows. It reports structural connection importance and different wall/window contributions by band; source context is aircraft/blast/supersonic low-frequency sound.
records.applicability: Supports treating airborne and structure-coupled routes as coexisting hypotheses. Lab assemblies and source spectra differ from this unknown building; no result transfers as a prediction.

records.title: Norén-Cosgriff et al., Countermeasures against noise and vibrations in lightweight wooden buildings caused by outdoor sources with strong low-frequency components
records.released_version: Noise Control Engineering Journal, vol. 64, issue 6, pp. 737–752, 2016; DOI 10.3397/1/376416.
records.locator: SINTEF publication record: abstract, author list, year, project methods and reported field outcomes.
records.observed_operation: Opened the authors' institution publication page and read the abstract and bibliographic details.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Program combined lab measurements, finite-element simulation, countermeasure design, and full-scale field tests in a typical Norwegian wooden building under F-16 aircraft noise. It measured both indoor A-weighted sound and floor vibration.
records.applicability: Useful precedent for measuring sound and vibration together and for mechanism review only. Aircraft source, wooden test building, and tested structural interventions differ; reported numerical reductions are not transferable and no construction is proposed.

records.title: Vargas Vera, San Millán-Castillo & Swerdlow, Sound insulation design methodology: case study on a music rehearsal room
records.released_version: Acoustics in Practice, vol. 7, no. 1, 2019; 10-page PDF; EAA publisher archive, no DOI identified in the accessed record.
records.locator: PDF abstract and methodology sections; repeated-source-cycle discussion; case measurements/modelling and scope/conclusion re verification.
records.observed_operation: Opened the EAA-hosted primary PDF and read text from the paper.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: A residential-house basement rehearsal-room case tested bass guitar, guitar and drums, using repeated 20-second passages and measured source power/site airborne insulation before modeling proposals. The paper states its proposal scope leaves verification of the proposed solutions out.
records.applicability: Closest source/profile and workflow comparator found; does not demonstrate successful installed treatment, include this building's construction, or settle structural transmission.

records.title: Støfringsdal & Bolstad, Optimizing (too) small ensemble rehearsal rooms for acoustic loud music
records.released_version: Proceedings of the Institute of Acoustics, vol. 45, part 2, Auditorium Acoustics 2023; DOI 10.25144/16014.
records.locator: PDF introduction, section on the professional wind-band rehearsal room and prior absorption/refurbishment, and reported musician survey/performance findings.
records.observed_operation: Retrieved the official Institute of Acoustics proceedings PDF/search record and read the paper's source excerpts.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The detailed case is a 1,600 m³ professional wind-band rehearsal room. Earlier repeated changes included 40 mm porous wall/ceiling absorbers; musicians reported a too-dry, imbalanced room and difficulty hearing one another. The article concerns internal rehearsal acoustics and a completed redesign.
records.applicability: A real implementation-history lead and warning about internal tradeoffs from absorption, not an exterior isolation precedent; room scale and ensemble differ.

records.title: Shearer, Dance, Gomez-Agustina & Randell, Flexible control of acoustic conditions in a music rehearsal space using airbeds
records.released_version: Applied Acoustics, vol. 173, article 107708, published February 2021; DOI 10.1016/j.apacoust.2020.107708.
records.locator: London South Bank University author research record and abstract; linked publisher article.
records.observed_operation: Opened the authors' university research portal, read the abstract and publication details.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Laboratory tests selected an inflated consumer airbed model, then room-acoustic measurements compared the former church Henry Wood Hall before/after installation to reduce lower-band reverberation for a flexible orchestral/voice rehearsal use.
records.applicability: Interesting low-cost, reversible room-decay approach; its measured target is internal reverberation, not sound transmission to homes/courtyard.

records.title: BKL Consultants, UBC Music Building Renovations case record
records.released_version: Project completed 2022; page states copyright 2024; no revision/commit identifier shown.
records.locator: Consultant case page: project scope, before/construction visits, measured paths, structure-borne concern, completion and cost.
records.observed_operation: Opened the project acoustician's first-party case-study page and read the described project history.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Extensive first/second/fourth-floor institutional renovation; consultant reports pre-work sound-isolation measurements and instrument tests, a construction inspection, structure-borne concern, and a $2.8M capital project. No raw measurement records or numeric after-results are on this page.
records.applicability: Use as a lead for requesting measurement protocol, drawings and post-project data, not as a performance prediction for a small residential-edge site.

records.title: Sandy Brown, Clore Music Studios, New College, University of Oxford case record
records.released_version: Studios opened summer 2019; consultant web case record has no revision/commit identifier shown.
records.locator: Consultant project summary: area noise survey, music egress criteria, envelope / box-in-box design and interior room-mode treatment.
records.observed_operation: Opened the project's acoustic consultant case page and read the project summary and described implementation.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Purpose-built multiroom college facility in a three-storey solid-stone context. The consultant reports an environmental noise survey used to set plant/music egress limits, independent heavy structures, wide-airspace windows, floated floors and internal acoustic finishes. The page gives no numeric post-opening results.
records.applicability: Useful question template linking an outdoor baseline to an explicit receiver limit and design, but its purpose-built construction, scale, and historic setting are materially unlike the no-construction scope here.
